title: Single Responsibility Principle
description: Learn why each class should have one reason to change.

data.text: The **Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)** states that a class should have only one reason to change, meaning it should have only one job or responsibility.
When a class has multiple responsibilities, it becomes fragile. Changes to one responsibility may break the other functionality. SRP leads to more maintainable, testable, and reusable code.

data.title: Violating SRP

data.text: This class violates SRP because it handles report generation, file persistence, and email notification — three distinct responsibilities.

data.title: Following SRP

items: More testable with focused unit tests
Changes to one responsibility don't affect others

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: A class should have only one reason to change
SRP leads to more maintainable and testable code
data.takeaway: Apply SRP by identifying distinct responsibilities and separating them into focused classes.
